illustrae.name:
SEQUENCE :

IMAGE 1 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. A roughly circular tumor mass made mostly of small grey/blue bulk tumor cells packed together — the large majority. Scattered among them, only a FEW distinct larger magenta/purple cancer stem cells (CSCs), clearly the minority (e.g. 3–4 CSCs among ~40 bulk cells). Label the mass "pre-treatment tumor"; a small bracket or callout points to one magenta cell labeled "cancer stem cell (CSC)" and to the grey cells labeled "bulk tumor cells." The CSC:bulk ratio is visibly LOW. No molecular detail. Clean composition.

IMAGE 2 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. The same tumor mass, now with a treatment band/arrow sweeping across it from above labeled "chemotherapy." Many of the small grey/blue bulk cells are shown dying — faded, fragmenting, marked with small X's or dissolving outlines. The magenta/purple CSCs are shown UNHARMED, intact and brightly colored amid the dying bulk cells. A label: "bulk cells killed — CSCs survive." No drug structure, just the treatment arrow/band. Clean composition.

IMAGE 3 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. A much SMALLER tumor mass than frame 1 — most grey/blue bulk cells are gone. The same few magenta/purple CSCs remain, but now they make up a much LARGER PROPORTION of what's left (e.g. 3–4 CSCs among only ~6–8 surviving bulk cells). The tumor is smaller overall but visibly CSC-rich. Label "post-treatment tumor" and a callout: "tumor shrinks, but CSC fraction rises." The KEY READ is the proportion shift versus frame 1. No molecular detail. Clean composition.

IMAGE 4 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. The surviving magenta/purple CSCs now drawn QUIESCENT — muted/desaturated color, each with a small "pause" or sleep indicator (e.g. a small ‖ pause mark or closed/dormant outline), not dividing. Few or no bulk cells around them. A calm, sparse composition. Label "dormancy — CSCs quiescent" and a note "refractory to treatment." Convey stillness. No molecular detail. Clean composition.

IMAGE 5 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. The same CSCs now REACTIVATING — color returning to bright magenta/purple, the pause indicators gone, and each CSC shown beginning to divide (small outward budding arrows, one cell splitting into two). New small grey/blue bulk cells just starting to appear around them as the CSCs regenerate the population. Label "reactivation — CSCs resume dividing." Convey motion/restart. No molecular detail. Clean composition.

IMAGE 6 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. A regenerated tumor mass roughly the SIZE of the original pre-treatment tumor (frame 1) — bulk grey/blue cells have regrown — BUT the magenta/purple CSC fraction is now VISIBLY LARGER than in frame 1 (e.g. 7–8 CSCs among ~40 bulk cells, versus 3–4 before). A curved RETURN ARROW loops from this tumor back toward the pre-treatment position, labeled "next cycle starts with more CSCs." A small comparison cue: a faint side-by-side of the old small CSC fraction vs the new larger one, or a tick-up indicator. Label "relapse — regenerated, more resistant." The KEY READ: the cycle closes, but the tumor is worse. No molecular detail. Clean composition.

illustrae.name:
Sequence of events:

1 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. A horizontally-oriented mitochondrion in the center of the frame. On its outer membrane sit RED anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family blocks, labeled "Bcl-2 / Bcl-XL — anti-apoptotic (guarding)." From the upper-left, several small stress icons feed in with arrows, labeled "internal stress: DNA damage · hypoxia · chemotherapy · misfolded proteins." These activate GREEN pro-apoptotic Bcl-2 family shapes that push against the red blocks — a visible tug/opposition at the membrane, labeled "pro-apoptotic Bcl-2 members activated." A small label frames the moment: "the Bcl-2 family decision." No cytochrome c released yet. No chemical structures. Fill the wide frame: stress inputs on the left, mitochondrion center, red-vs-green tug on its membrane.

2 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. The same center mitochondrion, same style. The GREEN pro-apoptotic Bcl-2 members have now won: they form pores/openings in the mitochondrial OUTER MEMBRANE, shown as clear gaps or channel shapes, labeled "mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP)." The RED anti-apoptotic blocks are shown overwhelmed/displaced. Inside the mitochondrion, small ORANGE cytochrome c dots are visible, poised near the new openings but not yet released, labeled "cytochrome c (inside)." No apoptosome yet. No chemical structures. Fill the wide frame with the mitochondrion and the newly opened membrane.

3 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. The same center mitochondrion. ORANGE cytochrome c dots are now streaming OUT through the permeabilized outer membrane into the surrounding cytosol, shown with clear directional arrows, labeled "cytochrome c released into cytosol." A prominent, unmissable marker flags this beat: a bold badge or banner labeled "POINT OF NO RETURN — cell is now committed to die," positioned so it dominates the frame. A short clarifying note: "commitment happens HERE — not at caspase activation." No apoptosome yet — this panel is only the release and its significance. No chemical structures. Fill the wide frame: mitochondrion releasing orange cytochrome c, bold commitment marker.

4 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. Move to the cytosol beside the mitochondrion (mitochondrion still visible at the edge for continuity). ORANGE cytochrome c dots bind BLUE Apaf-1 adaptor shapes, labeled "cytochrome c + Apaf-1." They assemble into a distinct wheel-like/ring complex, labeled "apoptosome." At the hub of the apoptosome, an inactive enzyme shape labeled "procaspase-9" is shown converting into an active form labeled "caspase-9 (active)" with a small activation spark. No executioner cascade yet. No chemical structures. Fill the wide frame: cytochrome c meeting Apaf-1, the wheel-shaped apoptosome assembling, caspase-9 activating at its center.

5 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. On the left, "caspase-9 (active)" with an arrow to a group of executioner enzyme shapes labeled "caspase-3 · caspase-6 · caspase-7 (executioners)" — shown as an amplifying cascade (one arrow branching to several). On the right, a cell showing the three morphological hallmarks, each labeled: "chromatin condensation" (condensed dark nucleus), "DNA fragmentation" (broken DNA pieces), and "membrane blebbing" (bulging cell edge). No chemical structures. Fill the wide frame: caspase-9 → executioner cascade on the left, the dying cell with its three labeled hallmarks on the right.

6 - Landscape 1920×1080, clean white background, flat professional scientific-illustration style. The center mitochondrion again, but now guarded by an EXCESS of RED anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 blocks — many more than in panel 1, crowding the membrane, labeled "anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 overexpressed." The GREEN pro-apoptotic members are shown outnumbered and unable to open the membrane. Cytochrome c stays INSIDE the mitochondrion (orange dots contained), with a blocked/crossed arrow where release would occur, labeled "no cytochrome c release → apoptosis blocked." A second small icon shows a mutated pathway component with an X, labeled "or mutation disables the pathway." A summary label: "cancer evades apoptosis." No chemical structures. Fill the wide frame: over-guarded mitochondrion, contained cytochrome c, blocked death signal.
